chapter: Dreamland and the Tuxedo dance hall
title: Layout of 25s on Franklin Street: bar, booth and gambling room
summary: Manetta sketches the Franklin Street 25 club, with its bar, glass booth with a piano and the gambling room where Joe Oliver and Jelly Roll played pool and cards.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I don't quite understand the arrangement in 25s. When you come in the door, there's this big booth. Is that right?

Not yet. Now watch. I'll describe it. Here's Franklin Street. Mm-hmm. Here's the door. Right. As you go in the door, there's the bar. There, right to your left, that's where the booth is built. Oh, I see. Right from the door. Mm-hmm. Nice glass. You know it had glasses in it? Oh, I see. It's just a place. And the booth runs right at the edge of the counter, where you go right out from the bar, right back in the gambling room.
I see. So the bar was in the—just as you came in was the bar. There's the bar. And then you go on back and there's the—
Right. You just go right out the bar, right into the gambling room, where they had to sit, pool, and play cards. I see. Is it a card game?
Hmm? Cards? Cards? Yeah, cards. With cards? Yeah, with cards. Yeah, with cards.
You like poker? They have. Like, they played poker. They played five up and all different games like that. But the most of the game there was cards.
Mm-hmm.
That's a slick game, you know. Did you play it? No, indeed. I never gambled in my life. No? No, indeed.
Is that so?
Never gambled. Never had a pool stick in my hand.
Is that so?
Joe Oliver was a good pool player.
How about Jelly Roll?
Jelly Roll was a good pool player. He says so.
Somebody said—

He could shoot pool good, Jelly Roll. Them fellas was doing that all day long around it. They was around it all day. They were on the piano, back in the pool room, playing cards, and blackjack, everything.
Was the piano in the booths?
In the booth. A nice piano, too. They had a nice table in the booth, chairs.
But you could see into the booth from the bar then, through the glass.

Well, no, no, no. You couldn't see that as you entered, because they had a kind of bolted. It was hot, and the glass. The glass on top. Yeah. So you couldn't see the door. Now, like the door, when you go in the booth, they had a nice glass door. It was almost private. Like, you go in there, you could lock yourself there. No one couldn't get in there.
Did you see many girls in there?

Oh, sure. See all them women that used to come around and meet their men around there, go in the booths, and have a good time. Spend a lot of money in there. Get a fella to play piano, Jelly Roll, and them fellas, Birmingham and all them fellas like that. Give them chips and all like that.
How many tables were in there? How many tables were in the booths? Only one table.
Just one table?
One? Small room then.
Yeah, small. Well, about like this to that. Uh-huh. Well, a nice big piano in there. Pianos right as you come in the booth. Pianos right to your left.
How did you get the drinks in there? Did they have a waiter or-
Oh, you do. They had a bell in there. Just push the button. What does it bring them? Push the button.
Somebody look there.
There. Bar tentacle. Bar tentacle's right there. When you open that door there, there was the bar. Yeah.
